children: The German semiconductor maker is expanding its India R&D footprint with a new Bengaluru campus and a larger presence in Ahmedabad and Hyderabad.

Infineon Technologies has increased its India workforce by 28 per cent over the past year as the German semiconductor maker expands its research and development footprint in the country, CEO Jochen Hanebeck said at Semicon India.

The company, which has operated in India for more than 25 years, now employs more than 2,800 people across Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. It works with more than 1,200 customers in India, ranging from startups to large companies, as it seeks to deepen its role in the country's semiconductor ecosystem.
Infineon has expanded its global capability centre in Ahmedabad and strengthened its R&D presence in Hyderabad, while establishing a new state-of-the-art campus in Bengaluru, Hanebeck said.

The company's India operations contribute to global technology development and support customers worldwide, reflecting its broader strategy of using the country's engineering and technology capabilities beyond the domestic market. Hanebeck said India is increasingly contributing to innovation on a global scale across sectors. Hanebeck said Infineon sees India as a market of "tremendous importance", citing investment across digitalisation, electrification and automation as areas creating opportunities for semiconductor companies.
The company is also expanding its focus on developing semiconductor talent through partnerships with government institutions, customers, start-ups, universities and industry associations.

Infineon and NILIT launched a centre of excellence a day before Hanebeck's address to prepare the next generation of semiconductor engineers with industry-relevant skills. Hanebeck said the initiative is aimed at strengthening the talent base required for the industry's future.
India's Role In Global Chip Value Chain

Hanebeck said Infineon's confidence in India has strengthened as the company continues to expand its presence and deepen customer relationships. He said India has potential to strengthen its position across the global semiconductor value chain, with events such as Semicon India bringing together talent, technologies, partnerships and ideas needed for the industry's development.
Infineon said its India operations currently span Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, with the company continuing to invest in its local innovation footprint and customer relationships.
